portion_doctrine: Segments 21-30 of series_3_download.docx consist almost entirely of Adobe Photoshop tutorial transcripts. The content is pedagogical video demonstrations covering compositing principles, adjustment layers, blend modes, dynamic text in Photoshop 2026, light blur effects, and AI-powered removal tools. Stripped of timestamps, chat interactions, hosting preamble, and UI navigation descriptions, the real extractable content is Photoshop-specific tactic and method instructions. This is NOT strategic/business doctrine; it is technical tool training.
operating_rules: Perspective matching is foundational: horizon line alignment between foreground and background must match or composite fails, regardless of perfect masking/shadows/color
Atmospheric perspective: farther objects lose contrast, shift color toward sky (blue in daylight, warm in sunset), scale appears smaller
Matching brightness/contrast: use desaturate + levels/curves adjustment layers to verify tonal match before finalizing composite
Matching saturation: create saturation map using selective color (reds/greens/blues to -100, whites/blacks to +100) to see saturation distribution
Ambient color injection: duplicate background layer, blur, change blend mode to Color, reduce opacity; or use Curves with auto-color-pick to match shadows/highlights
Shadow anatomy: Umbra (core shape) + Penumbra (feathered edge) + Contact/Occlusion shadow (where object meets ground); all must be in perspective to vanishing point

Blend If technique: double-click layer to open Layer Style, adjust 'Blend If' sliders (current layer and underlying layer) to make areas invisible based on light/dark values; hold Alt to split sliders for feathering
Layer mask inversion: Alt+Click mask icon creates reverse mask; or Ctrl+I to invert existing mask
Dynamic text (Photoshop 2026): Block, Circle, Arch, Bow shapes; hold Ctrl+drag to move text around center; Control+Cmd+click on start/end points to adjust text span

Remove tool new feature: 'Find Distractions' AI categorizes all unwanted elements automatically (vehicles, poles, fixtures, vegetation, visual clutter), removes with single click if 'Create New Layer' is enabled
Path blur: multi-path support, adjustable speed slider; can create multiple blur paths in one operation for complex motion effects
Smart objects mandatory for non-destructive effects: convert layer to smart object before applying filters; allows double-click to re-edit blur/hue/saturation settings without re-rendering
Perspective Warp tool: grid-based perspective correction for objects with faces (crates, cars); cannot reliably warp organic forms (people)
named_methods: Jesus Ramirez composite bootcamp method: 6-step principle-based approach (Perspective, Atmospheric Perspective, Brightness Matching, Saturation Matching, Ambient Color, Shadows)
Layer style automation: Blend If for light-based masking without layer masks
Saturation map visualization: selective color -100 on all colors except whites/blacks at +100
Feathered blend transitions: Alt+split Blend If sliders for soft edges
Non-destructive color grading chain: Desaturate + Levels + Curves + Selective Color + Hue/Saturation stacked as clipped adjustment layers
Path blur multi-path workflow: click to add multiple blur vectors in single filter instance
Dynamic text with stroke overlay: duplicate text layer with fill opacity 0, add stroke on copy, create layer mask linking to hide/show behind subjects, link layers together to move as unit

Light blur composite workflow: remove background, blur background layer with path blur, duplicate subject, apply blur to copy, create masked layer to restore eyes/face focus, add texture overlay with screen blend mode

specific_tactics: Horizon line discovery: ignore detail, imagine ground plane and sky only, find where they meet visually
Cube visualization for perspective: mentally model any object (person, car, crate) as cube to determine horizon line position relative to object
Contact shadow placement: sits on ground plane at same perspective vanishing point as object; closer object to light source makes larger shadow
Ctrl+J duplicate shortcut to create copy for blending experiments
Ctrl+Alt+G (Cmd+Option+G Mac) to create clipping mask without layer panel gymnastics
Ctrl+Right/Left bracket to move layer up/down; Ctrl+Shift+Right/Left bracket to jump to top/bottom
Alt+Move tool drag to duplicate and move layer simultaneously
Hold Shift+Click layer to temporarily disable layer mask (to verify original underneath)
Double-click gray area of layer to open Layer Style dialog (faster than Layer > Layer Style menu)
Control+Cmd+T transform with reference point enabled: reference point on horizon line + Alt-drag to scale in perspective
Perspective Warp Shift+Click to constrain/straighten paired points
AI Remove: Check 'Sample All Layers' and 'Create New Layer' to ensure non-destructive result
Dynamic text UI challenge: Zoom way in to grab start/end point icons (difficult to select); Control+Cmd+drag to move center point easily
Layer mask chain icon: unlink layer from mask to move layer independently of mask boundaries
prompts: Does the horizon line match between foreground and background? If not, composite will feel wrong regardless of other perfection.
Can you see the top/bottom/sides of the object as a cube? This determines horizon line position.
When you desaturate the composite, do the contrast values match across the subject-background boundary?
Is the saturation map showing equal brightness in shadows and highlights on both subject and background?
What color is bouncing onto the subject from the environment? (Ambient color presence test)
Do shadows have both Umbra and Penumbra, plus contact shadow on ground plane?
Can Blend If do this job faster than a layer mask? (Light-based masking is Blend If's use case)
Is this layer effect meant to be adjustable later? If yes, convert to smart object first.

contradictions: Blend If vs Layer Mask: Blend If presented as faster for light-based masking, but layer masks offer more pixel-level control. No guidance on when to use which.
Neural Harmonization Filter vs Manual Color Matching: Shown as alternative to curves/selective color, but user expressed lack of control preference. No reconciliation of speed vs precision trade-off.

Smart Objects and Perspective Warp: Perspective Warp requires rasterization before scaling example, contradicting non-destructive best practice; no clarity on when rasterization is mandatory vs optional.
weird_gold: Cube visualization for horizon line: thinking of any object as a cube reveals horizon line position instantly without mathematical vanishing point tracing; this is perceptual shortcut vs technical accuracy
Contact shadow placement rule: Contact shadow sits on ground plane at perspective vanishing point, not directly under object; this is counterintuitive but critical for realism

Saturation map selective color formula: Reds/Greens/Blues to -100 on all, then Whites to +100, Blacks to +100; creates grayscale where white = saturated, black = desaturated. This is a hidden feature most don't know.

Dynamic text layer linking: linking two text layers (one behind, one in front of subject) together allows single move operation that preserves relative positioning; clever workaround for split-layer text effects
Alt+Split Blend If sliders: one keystroke (Alt) converts hard transition to feathered transition by splitting single slider into two independent points; most users never discover this
Path Blur multi-path in one filter: can draw multiple blur vectors in single filter instance without closing/reopening, enables complex motion trails

Remove Tool auto-detection: AI categorizes distraction types (vehicles, poles, vegetation, fixtures, visual clutter) automatically; user only has to click 'Select All' for one-click removal of mixed distraction types
